title: Roman Abramovich plans to defy UK government with charity foundation for frozen Chelsea sale funds
content:
Roman Abramovich is planning to defy the UK government by using a new charitable foundation in an attempt to break the current impasse regarding the frozen £2.35billion from the sale of Chelsea.

The new foundation, which needs to be registered with the Charity Commission and will be overseen by Mike Penrose, a former UNICEF executive, is due to outline Abramovich’s intention for the money to be spent on global causes as opposed to being limited to Ukraine.

This is in contrast to the UK government’s stance regarding how the proceeds from the sale are spent, as it has long maintained that the £2.35bn ($3.12bn at current rates) will remain frozen unless the Russian billionaire signs off on it only being spent in Ukraine.

The UK government, then led by Conservative Prime Minister Boris Johnson, forced Abramovich to sell Chelsea after Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022. He was also sanctioned and had his assets frozen.

Blue-Co, a consortium led by Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital, bought the club in May 2022, but Abramovich’s proceeds of the sale have remained frozen.

In December, UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer threatened Abramovich with legal action unless the Russian oligarch agrees to the government’s conditions, adding that the “clock is ticking”.

Abramovich’s representatives, however, have long maintained it was never part of the agreement for the proceeds to only be spent in Ukraine — and now they are trying to break the deadlock by utilising the new foundation without the government’s permission.

“Our understanding is that a foundation is currently in the process of being registered, which we welcome,” a spokesperson for Abramovich told The Athletic. “Mr Abramovich maintains his intention to donate funds to humanitarian causes once the relevant legal obstacles are resolved.”

The application for the new foundation, which is due to be named the Foundation for Victims of Conflict, is set to be submitted this week.

“I can confirm that I am preparing a submission to the Charity Commission to register a new foundation dedicated to supporting victims of conflict worldwide,” Penrose said in a statement.

“I am confident in the strength of the board I have assembled, which brings together individuals with significant experience in humanitarian work across the globe.

“The application will be submitted this week. The foundation’s objectives are aligned with those set out in the deed of undertaking, and we are hopeful that, once the relevant legal matters are resolved, the foundation will be in a position to receive a donation.”

The Athletic previously reported on how Abramovich’s legal team informed the UK government that the proceeds from the Chelsea sale are “wholly” his and that he would fight any attempt to confiscate them.

In correspondence seen by The Athletic, the former Chelsea owner’s lawyers also said that the “UK Government appears to be treating this proposed donation as a form of punitive measure against Mr Abramovich”.

Central to the dispute is the ongoing investigation into the Russian in Jersey, which included more than $7bn worth of Abramovich-linked assets being seized by the Jersey Royal Court in March 2022.

The Athletic has contacted the UK government and Charity Commission for comment.
